sentences.text:
1 This Court while granting interim protection vide order dated 02.02.2023 has passed the following order:-
"The applicant has moved the present application under Section 438 of Cr.P.C.
praying for grant of anticipatory bail in Case Crime No.466 of 2020 under sections 406, 420, 504, 506, I.P.C., P.S. Indira Nagar, district Lucknow.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant who is permitted to implead the complainant during course of the day, and learned A.G.A. for the State.
It is submitted on behalf of the applicant that the incident is of 2016.
Application under section 156(3) CrPC has been given in the year 2020 after delay of four years without any plausible explanation.
The complainant and Suresh Agarwal both were together doing property business.

In 2014, when the applicant was in need of money,
he contacted Suresh Agarwal and the complainant to sell his plot.
A consideration amount of Rs.6 lacs was paid by them and on the saying of the complainant, he transferred his land to Suresh Agarwal.
It is submitted that the dispute is purely civil in nature.
It is next submitted that He further submits that the applicant has cooperated in the investigation.
Charge sheet has been filed.
He undertakes to cooperate in the trial.
Learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer made by the applicant's counsel.
He is allowed fifteen days' time to file objections.
Issue notice to respondent No.4.
List on 3.3.2023.

Without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case and considering the nature of accusation and having no criminal antecedents, the undertaking given on behalf of the applicant that he shall cooperate in the trial and gravity of offence, I am of the opinion that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail in this case in the light of judgment of Supreme Court in Sushila Aggarwal and others vs. State (NCT of Delhi)
and another (2020)5 SCC 1, subject to her cooperation in the trial.
